name: JhaJi Store
tagline: Homemade Mithila pickles from Darbhanga, Bihar
excerpt: JhaJi Achaar left Shark Tank India Season 1 without a deal, then won investment from Namita Thapar and Vineeta Singh months later.
content:
JhaJi sells traditional homemade pickles from the Mithila region of Bihar, made with family recipes. Sisters-in-law Kalpana Jha and Uma Jha started it from Darbhanga and pitched in the fourth episode of Shark Tank India, aired on 23 December 2021.

They left without a deal. But the story did not end there: a study of company filings found that JhaJi was one of two rejected Season 1 businesses that later got shark money, with Namita Thapar and Vineeta Singh investing ₹30 lakh in September 2022.

Inc42's filing data shows revenue growing in FY25, with a small loss.

faq.q: Did JhaJi get a deal on Shark Tank India?
faq.a: Not on the show. Namita Thapar and Vineeta Singh invested later, in September 2022.
Yes. It filed accounts for FY25 and sells through its own website.
Inc42's filing data shows total revenue of about ₹9.7 crore in FY25.

lessons: Our analysis: a 'no' on TV is not final; following up with traction can turn sharks into investors later.
Our analysis: authentic regional food with a founder story travels well online.
notes: Ask (₹50 lakh for 10%) appears only on Wikipedia/blogs (a YourStory piece could not be fetched), so it is left out. Post-show amount conflicts: The Federal/PrivateCircle says ₹30 lakh (Sept 2022); Wikipedia and blogs say ₹85 lakh for 8.45% with Jharkhand Angels when they returned in Season 2; Inc42 Datalabs shows total funding $1.57M+. Episode 4 is confirmed by SET India's synopsis ('chemical-free pickle brand').
